approaches.name: digital ambassador training and public middle-mile fiber for rural connectivity
approaches.description: Trains local Digital Ambassadors to deliver internet safety training and builds public middle-mile fiber where private investment is unviable. Practices: Digital Ambassadors train-the-trainer digital literacy delivery; public middle-mile fiber network enabling private ISP retail expansion.
approaches.why_innovative: New delivery arrangement: local trainers mobilize and train communities - cue: 'train-the-trainer' | category Collaborative; adoption apply; judged in 1 round(s); final check: digital core, in_use before 2019

evidence.text: Furthermore, the DAIP has trained 3,500 people, adopting a train-the-trainer approach in its implementation by leveraging local talent (as ‘Digital Ambassadors’) in the connected municipalities to deliver trainings and contribute to beneficiary mobilization.

extra_evidence.text: Other digital literacy projects like the EU- funded Rural Development through Digital Inclusion (REDI) program are using these trainers for follow-up activities, ensuring continued support to rural communities.

As a middle mile network aiming to provide access to fiber optic middle mile infrastructure to rural settlements that are financially unviable for the private sector, the Parent and AF Project enable private capital by: (i) stimulating parallel expansion of middle mile fiber optic networks to the more viable rural areas, given that least viable are being covered by the ON network;

(ii) expansion of retail networks by ISPs and mobile operators to connect people and businesses in connected rural settlements; and (iii) upgrading retail network infrastructure for existing subscribers.
As a result of the Parent Project’s effective implementation, an additional US$ 20 million of private sector investment is estimated to be enabled – see annex 2 for details.20 C.

category.rationale: Collaborative: local actors deliver training, not a new technology

sector.rationale: Digital literacy training delivered via connected municipalities, serving the broadband/digital infrastructure project's adoption goals.

approaches.name: underground middle-mile fiber network with Ookla speed monitoring
approaches.description: Deploys ~1,200 km of underground middle-mile fiber to rural settlements and uses Ookla subnational data to monitor broadband speeds. Practices: underground fiber deployment as climate-resilience measure; middle mile fiber network to 79 rural settlements; Ookla subnational data for broadband speed monitoring.
approaches.why_innovative: New process: climate-resilient underground cable routing - cue: 'climate-smart' | category Technological; adoption apply; judged in 1 round(s); final check: digital core, in_use before 2019

evidence.text: For example, to mitigate the risks of landslides or high snowfall in mountainous areas, the network is deployed underground (at higher cost) instead of aerially.

extra_evidence.text: A major telecom operator in Georgia faced a country-wide outage in January 2025 due to damage to cross-border links with Türkiye, with heavy snowfall limiting repair capabilities.29 As such, the project will continue to deploy underground fiber as a climate resilience measure to mitigate the risk of leaving rural population unconnected due to snowstorms, landslides or flash floods.

More specifically, the AF will finance the remaining network in Eastern Georgia by deploying the middle mile connectivity to the areas of Kvemo Kartli, Samtskhe-Javakheti, Mtskheta-Mtianeti, and Kakheti to cover 79 rural settlements, requiring approximately 1,200 km of middle mile infrastructure, completing the pan-national network in all regions as designed.
Proceeds of the AF will be utilized to complete extending access to broadband services coutrywide as per the Open Net Program.
Toward this end, bulk of the AF will supplement Component 1 alloction supporting both Passive Infrastructure Development and Active Infrastructure Procurement.
